speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) how many bird-related complaints have been received in the past three years; (b) what is being done to solve the problem of birds invading hawker centres to feed on leftover food; and (c) what is the Ministry doing to curb the bird population in the heartland estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The birds are attracted to hawker centres due to the availability of food.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Food scraps left behind will also create public health issues if they attract pests, such as cockroaches and rats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NEA has also been encouraging patrons to return their trays and crockery to the tray-return stations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These measures help to reduce the pet problem of birds feeding on leftover food in hawker centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The gel was found to be effective in the block where it was tested, and AVA has shared the solution with other interested stakeholders who may be keen to adopt such a measure.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Most importantly, the public has a role to play in curbing the bird population by maintaining the cleanliness of the overall environment and to not feed the birds.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: To this end, AVA, NEA and Town Councils are working together to educate residents not to litter or to feed the birds, through advisories, posters and even through grassroots events.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: NEA will take enforcement action against any offenders who do not comply.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have given feedback many times that there are a lot of pigeons along Mass Rapid Transit lines.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Despite that,  the population of pigeons is still a lot.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Early last year, there was a new fogging method that was used for the mynahs in Nee Soon South.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, it did not work out and, after that, it just stopped there.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First of all, on the issue of pigeons, there is no one-size-fits-all method and it is going to be multifactorial in terms of why the birds come back.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Part of the key reason is that they are attracted by leftover food.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The approach has to be through multi-faceted engagement with multiple stakeholders, chief of all, our residents, to make sure they do not throw food out of the window from the kitchen, and also to make sure that we cut down on littering.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Close the bins, this is a simple measure, but it is easier said than done.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have all experienced difficulties with these in our own estates as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, public education is important and that is the only way to reduce the source that will attract the birds to come.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Otherwise, no degree of culling, no degree of using gels or contraceptives, will stop the birds from coming back.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As for other methods to deal with the mynah issue, other than the gel that I illustrated before, the other trial that AVA has done in 2016 was to use the fogging method that was tried out in the Member's area before.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The result of that is still ongoing; the effectiveness is probably patchy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it also has to depend on how the fogging is done and the frequency as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The trial is still ongoing to figure out what is the most optimal way to apply it, what is the most optimal frequency of using that method.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The other alternative, for example, will be to use oral contraceptives.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This was used in the context of managing the pigeon population.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Such a trial has been shown to work in, for example, Italy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, the efficacy is only observed after a period of five years on a trial involving about 100 pigeons.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As you can imagine, oral contraceptive takes a longer lead time to work, because you are trying to prevent multiplication of the population, but the current population will still be around for some time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, you do not see an observable effect in the near term.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For mynahs or crows, for example, if they are more aggressive and they attack humans, one of the other options that has been applied before is to actually use arms to cull them because they can pose an immediate threat to humans by attacking humans.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the pigeons, they are usually more mild and they do not attack humans directly.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we can try other avenues before we take culling as the final option.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For the pigeons in the Khatib area, it is beyond education.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: There are people who feed them and I would urge stricter enforcement action.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For the mynah, I was told that it is not effective, not successful, and they have called it off.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And residents have been complaining about the population of mynahs and lots of noise that affect their living environment as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Perhaps the Minister of State could find out from his officer.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: What I was told is different from his reply.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the trial results, we will continue to review the efficacy and, at some point, we will make adjustments, if need be, and we will communicate to the Member accordingly.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I was wondering, in light of his earlier reply to the Parliamentary Question, saying that chickens carry a higher risk of transmitting bird flu compared to other birds like mynahs, surely the number of birds would matter as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I was wondering from the Ministry of National Development's (MND's) viewpoint, is there a threshold for the size of the flock at which this risk would increase to the public?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: If so, would MND consider taking additional measures and a more active approach to managing the bird pest issue in estates, such as Clementi, where I serve?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the bird population, as opposed to free-ranging chickens, the difference is this: birds do fly around, they can shift from one place to another quite quickly.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is not so easy as catching chickens which can only run around on the ground.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in terms of managing the bird population, the challenge is much more difficult compared to managing a few chickens running around in one fixed locality.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If you want a perfectly safe environment, then, yes, we should go all out, all guns blazing, and remove every single bird from the sky of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But Members know that that is not a practical approach and it is not always going to be as easily achieved.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: You can cull a thousand birds today, tomorrow another thousand will fly in from somewhere else.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is something that we have to take a very practical view and escalate when necessary.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I have two questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The first one is that I understand we do not have enough enforcement on the ground to catch the recalcitrants or the offenders.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, are there better methods to work around this because maybe the penalties are not stiff enough and we should review the penalties in place?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The second one is with regard to the population of the birds.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In certain locations, we have seen that the birds actually only nest or tend to frequent around certain types of trees.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Have there been any co-relationship studies done to see whether the type of trees planted results in the kind of population of birds that come around?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That has been used in some estates as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I know – I use it in my estate to catch people who are feeding or throwing rubbish out of their windows.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That has sometimes produced a good deterrent effect on the rest of the blocks from doing the same thing.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I urge the Member to work with NEA and see if deployment of such surveillance cameras to catch the culprit in the act would be useful to send a deterrent signal.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the population of birds in correlation to the types of trees, I do not have information on that.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I can surmise that, actually, birds can find any place to just rest.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, regardless of the tree type, if there is something that attracts them like a source of food, for example, they will still go there and they can actually rest on the tree, no matter what type of tree that is.
